title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with at most one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each pair evaluated a single shared_initial candidate under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and model, single‑shot generation was near ceiling, limiting observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with the study id to support replication and follow‑up experiments that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, or repair budget.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are widely proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Operators require semantic guarantees—sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation—that cannot be assessed by syntax alone. Hybrid architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) are therefore advocated to reduce operational risk. However, the practical value of these scaffolds depends critically on (a) what is held fixed when comparing pipelines (the estimand), (b) the single‑shot quality of the generator, (c) the validator's expressive coverage, and (d) the allowed repair budget.

Motivated by two methodological gaps in prior work—mixing verifier rescue with gains from independent resampling, and limited public benchmarks emphasizing semantic correctness—we preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to isolate the deterministic rescue utility that a validator plus a bounded automated repair can achieve when confronted with a single LLM candidate per intent. Our central research question asks: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate unchanged? We report a fully archived execution and analysis bundle that includes deterministic validator traces, provider call accounting, and the single repaired episode.
sections.related_work:
The literature shows active development of LLMs and agentic frameworks for NetOps, including intent translation, configuration synthesis, and repair [https://openalex.org/W4406484968; https://openalex.org/W4411015066; https://openalex.org/W4415275309]. Planner‑centric and tool‑augmented architectures (ReAct variants, planner frameworks) explicitly enable validators and external tools to correct or check generative outputs [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40676; https://openalex.org/W4389518608]. Empirical reports indicate that validator‑assisted generation can reduce errors, but success rates are dataset‑dependent and hinge on validator coverage [https://openalex.org/W4416927413; https://openalex.org/W4404240614]. Surveys and user studies additionally highlight practitioner caution about deploying LLM outputs without strong semantic guarantees [https://openalex.org/W7167855398; https://openalex.org/W4416927413].

Two methodological themes informed our design. First, many prior comparisons allow independent additional model draws when the validator fails; such resampling conflates estimator effects (more draws) with deterministic verifier rescue. Second, public benchmarks that focus on semantic correctness (reachability, policy compliance) remain limited, making controlled comparisons sensitive to task generation choices [https://openalex.org/W4415071524; https://openalex.org/W4392875514]. Our paired, shared_initial conditioning addresses the first gap by measuring only the deterministic rescue achievable without extra independent draws.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered under id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 and froze the primary estimand: the absolute paired difference in the proportion of unflagged verifier passes (guarded minus baseline) evaluated on pairs that share the identical initial LLM candidate. The preregistration specified the confirmatory hypothesis (H1), a paired design, inclusion/exclusion rules, multiplicity plan, contamination controls, and the analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1. All frozen design artifacts (prompts, executor inputs, analysis scripts) are archived in the run bundle.

Task generation and difficulty strata. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 into a synthetic_topology_suite_v1 and stratified into low/medium/high difficulty (100 tasks per stratum) using generator metadata fields such as changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, and required_command_count. Representative patterns include "shutdown_configure_restore" (medium) and "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change" (hard). The task manifest and representative task entries (six shown) are included in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and the run bundle.

Modeling, orchestration, and shared_initial conditioning. The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). To measure deterministic verifier rescue only, the pipeline produces a single shared_initial generation per pair (one model call per task) and evaluates two deterministic treatments on that same candidate: baseline—accept without modification; guarded—run deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and, if flagged, permit at most one automated repair attempt before final revalidation. This shared_initial protocol excludes benefits from independent resampling or verifier‑guided multiple draws by experimental design.

Validator, scoring, and repair policy. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implements the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: it checks sequencing requirements (must_be_down_for_fields), preservation of unspecified state, required_command_count, encoded reachability invariants for the synthetic topology, and forbidden‑template protections for protected_interfaces. Scoring is binary per preregistration: unflagged == pass; flagged after allowed repair == failure. The guarded repair policy allowed a single automated repair call (repair budget ≤1) designed to perform a localized corrective edit; repair provider traces and validator rechecks are recorded. The low‑level repair transcript for the single repaired episode is archived in the run bundle for forensic inspection.

Pilot, stopping, and missingness handling. The preregistration described an optional pilot (n = 60) for estimating discordance and calibrating power; that pilot was not executed and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed. Confirmatory main run planned 300 pairs (600 episodes) and a stopping rule that required 300 analyzable pairs after application of exclusion rules. Per preregistration, pairs are excluded only if both condition calls fail due to provider/infrastructure outage; no such exclusions occurred. Single‑call failures are retained and handled by the registered executor; none were observed. These handling rules and missingness summaries are archived (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter completed the confirmatory run: completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, and model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair). Deterministic reconciliation records stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 300, repair: 1}, cache_miss_count = 301, and no failed model calls. Missingness and contamination summaries record zero exclusions and zero flagged contamination episodes (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; analysis/contamination_summary.csv). All execution manifests and provider call audits are archived in execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl.

Marginal and paired outcomes. Marginal summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) show baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966666667 and guarded = 300/300 = 1.0. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11=299, n10=1 (guarded‑only), n01=0 (baseline‑only), n00=0. Confirmatory analysis (paired_binary_analysis_v1) produced absolute paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993, exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0, and a 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] with bootstrap_seed = 1729 and B = 10000. Per‑stratum outcomes were: low = 100/100 baseline & guarded; medium = 100/100 baseline & guarded; high = baseline 99/100 vs guarded 100/100, accounting for the single discordant episode.

Rescue diagnostic and repair trace. The single discordant pair (n10 = 1) invoked the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial flag to a sequencing omission: the shared_initial candidate omitted a required 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change (a must_be_down_for_fields violation per the task payload). The automated repair inserted the missing sequencing command and the validator returned valid == true. The repair provider trace, validator before/after snapshots, and normalized configuration strings are archived (execution/scoring/task-00000*-guarded.json entries and the low‑level repair trace); we report here the concise semantic summary (sequencing omission corrected) rather than verbatim provider transcripts.

Statistical interpretation. The observed near‑ceiling baseline produced only a single discordant pair (m = n10 + n01 = 1), so inference sensitivity was dominated by the scarcity of discordant observations rather than overall N. The exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 reflects the paucity of discordant evidence under the shared_initial estimand; the paired bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute paired improvement at ≤1 percentage point in this experimental context. These results do not imply equivalence under different estimand choices (for example, allowing resampling or expanding repair budget) or on different task distributions.
sections.discussion:
Estimator conditioning and operational interpretation. The shared_initial estimand intentionally conditions on a single LLM draw per intent and therefore measures only deterministic validator/repair rescue applied to that single candidate. This corresponds to production workflows that normatively perform one model call and rely on deterministic auditing and bounded automated repair before deployment. It excludes verifier benefits that arise when operations permit multiple independent model draws, iterative verifier‑guided generation, or human‑in‑the‑loop reruns; those alternative estimands should be evaluated separately because they change both the operational cost model and the rescue opportunity set.

Ceiling effects, power, and the unexecuted pilot. The preregistered power target assumed appreciable baseline discordance (target detectable absolute improvement 0.10 at α = 0.05, power ≈ 0.8). The optional pilot (n = 60) intended to estimate discordance and inform sample sizing was not executed; accordingly no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed. The observed baseline success (299/300) demonstrates a ceiling effect in this synthetic suite and limits sensitivity to small absolute improvements; future confirmatory designs should run the preregistered pilot to estimate discordance under the intended sampling frame and adjust N or estimand accordingly.

Validator coverage and external validity. The deterministic validator checked sequencing, required_command_count, preservation of unspecified state, encoded reachability invariants, and forbidden‑template protections. In this synthetic suite sequencing omissions were the predominant failure mode; other failure classes (reachability or forbidden‑template violations) were rare or absent. External validity is therefore limited: different generators, real production topologies, or a different model family may produce different failure‑mode distributions that change the marginal utility of a guarded pipeline.

Operational recommendations. When evaluating scaffolds for production, explicitly map the deployed operational procedure to the estimand under test. If operations rely on one model call per intent, the shared_initial analysis here is directly relevant and shows that deterministic audit plus a bounded automated repair can correct localized sequencing omissions. If operations permit resampling or iterative repair, evaluate those estimands separately because they can materially increase rescue probability. To increase rescue capacity, practitioners may expand repair budgets, permit resampling, or employ stronger domain‑tuned generators.

Reproducibility, artifacts, and deterministic reconciliation. All preregistration documents, task manifests, model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json), raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, analysis CSVs (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv), deterministic reconciliation, and analysis logs (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived in the run bundle. Deterministic reconciliation confirms consistent episode accounting, provider call audit counts (hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, completed = 301, failed = 0), and stage_counts; these artifacts permit independent re‑execution of the confirmatory calculations. Analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729) and the exact executor outputs are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity for small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release the preregistration id, execution and analysis artifacts, representative task manifests, and validator traces in the archived run bundle to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary estimand choice, model strength, or repair strategies.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition.
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
